handWritten.note: Written by hand after the runs, from the phases below: handWritten only. The harness writes every other field (merge() in scripts/cdp-m2-05-handoff.mjs); platform is a constant of that harness, not a measurement. Each phase records its commit, whether the product tree was clean, and the SHA-256 of the exe and of the engine binary.
handWritten.summary: Final pass on M2-05, on the build of 16e9e5c (exe 5336f6aa…, engine 39a97806…, Muse 1.4.2), in the app's isolated test mode, 1 live turn. A move to a new worktree that does not happen now removes that worktree and its muse/ branch and says so: refused while A responds (f-lock), failed on a held file (f-held-tracked, f-held-untracked), refused as a conflict (f-case-rename). The folder lock is checked at the preview, before the question and any worktree (f-lock). A file another program holds open is named as the cause (f-held-*). The Worktree -> Local return is byte-identical on this build (f-round-trip). A staged case-only rename stays refused: a known limit, no data loss.

items.1 new worktree of a move that does not h: f-lock: C's question was open when A's turn started. At A's first card, C's OK made a new worktree, handoff_move (newWorktree true) was refused because A was responding, and that worktree went with its branch; the banner ends 'the new worktree .muse\worktrees\repo-… was removed with its branch muse/repo-…, as nothing was left in it'. C's Move again, A still responding: refused at the preview ('The move could not be prepared: a conversation is still responding in this folder: stop it before moving'), no question, no worktree, no handoff_move. 0 events on Local's files, Local byte-identical, no branch, checkout or ref left. f-held-tracked, f-held-untracked and f-case-rename: each move that did not happen removed its new worktree and branch, and said so.
items.2 file in use: f-held-tracked: src/app.txt held open (FileShare.Read): 'both sides were restored as they were: src/app.txt is in use by another program: close it, then move again (error: unable to unlink old 'src/app.txt': Invalid argument)'. f-held-untracked: 'notes/local.md is in use by another program: close it, then move again (Git could not delete notes/local.md)'. Before: Git's 'Invalid argument' alone (c-held-tracked in m2-05-handoff-complement.json).
items.3 Worktree -> Local return: f-round-trip, on the final exe: A's work (5 changed files, 3 untracked, 1 ignored) went Local -> new worktree -> Local through the UI, OK each time. Local byte-identical to before; both sides hashed at each step (before, away, home); the worktree back to its checkout; 2 snapshot refs per move. Staging arrives unstaged, as the question says ('A  added.txt' -> '?? added.txt').
items.4 evidence corrections: m2-05-handoff-complement.json: forgedInputs names the c-start folder dialog answered by the harness's IPC interceptor. m2-05-handoff.json: handWritten.fields adds phases.setup.commit and phases["confirm-defect"].codeCommit, and its note says which fields the harness wrote. scripts/cdp-m2-05-handoff.mjs: the confirm-defect comment no longer blames dialog:allow-confirm. docs/SPEC.md, and m2-05-handoff.json's summary and forgedInputs: the preview and a refused move write none of the user's files, Git writing only inside .git. Every phase here records the engine's SHA-256.
items.5 case-only rename: Known limit, no data loss (f-case-rename; test handoff_refuses_a_case_only_rename_before_any_write). 'git mv README.md Readme.md' staged in Local: the preview of a new worktree has nothing to conflict with yet, so the question shows; on OK the move is refused as a conflict on both names, nothing written in Local (0 events, bytes and status unchanged, the rename still staged, no ref), and the new worktree removed. Not fixed: on a disk that ignores case, Git does not see an unstaged case-only rename (core.ignorecase), and every move's staging arrives unstaged, so letting it move would drop the rename silently. Commit it first.

fixes.defect: A refused or failed move to a new worktree left that worktree and its muse/ branch behind, unannounced (<worktree c>, <worktree 2>, <worktree 3> in m2-05-handoff-complement.json). The folder lock was checked only after the question and the worktree's creation.
fixes.after: The renderer tells handoff_move it created the target (newWorktree). When the move does not happen, that worktree and its branch go while they are as created: nothing in the folder but its checkout, ignored files included, and no commit Local's HEAD lacks. Otherwise they stay and the message says why. handoff_preview refuses as the move would. Tests: a_move_is_refused_before_its_question_while_the_folder_answers and a_refused_move_removes_the_worktree_made_for_it (both failing without the fix), a_move_that_did_not_happen_removes_the_worktree_made_for_it, a_worktree_made_for_a_move_stays_while_it_holds_anything, handoff.test.ts. Live: f-lock, f-held-*, f-case-rename.

fixes.defect: With a tracked Local file held open by another program, the move said only Git's 'unable to unlink old 'src/app.txt': Invalid argument'.
fixes.after: When a step fails, its files are opened for DELETE with every sharing mode: a sharing violation means another program holds the file, and the message leads with '<file> is in use by another program: close it, then move again'. The guessed '(in use by another program?)' is gone. Test (Windows): handoff_names_a_tracked_file_another_program_holds_open, failing without the fix. Live: f-held-tracked, f-held-untracked.

forgedInputs: A and C were started by a direct start_session each (no turn), adopted on a reload (f-start). C cannot be A's Fork conversation on this host (MSP -32023 forkBoundaryInvalid, docs/upstream); A's live turn went through its own composer.
The TaskDialog's buttons are pressed with TDM_CLICK_BUTTON, as in the earlier records. In f-lock, C's question was read, left open, and answered once A's first card waited.
Held files: a separate PowerShell process opens them with FileShare.Read and no delete sharing, as an editor or viewer does.
Besides start_session, no native command was called directly: every move and refusal went through the UI. The harness reads pending approvals with list_pending_requests.
limits: Between the preview and the move a turn can still start in the folder (f-lock): the move is then refused after the question, and the worktree made for it goes.
A worktree created for a move goes only when the move does not happen; after a move it stays, like any worktree.
Naming a file in use relies on Windows sharing modes; elsewhere Git can delete or replace an open file.
A staged case-only rename is refused as a conflict (item 5): the wording says 'would conflict' where the remedy is to commit it first.
The model's shell still reports the folder in the \\?\ form (#88).
history: f-case-rename first ran answering Cancel, on the assumption that the preview already sees the conflict. For a new worktree it cannot, the worktree not existing yet: the question showed and Cancel moved nothing, Local unchanged. The recorded run answers OK.
f-lock's prompt is the complement's step 1 text, reused as is.
liveTurnsDetail: f-lock: A in Local, shell Get-Location (one card, Allow once), while C's move ran into the lock.
